Revised assessment: The statement’s tone is broadly supportive but balanced. Under the Fed’s average-inflation-targeting regime (Powell’s 2020 Jackson Hole shift; “makeup strategy”), keeping the funds rate at 0–0.25% and continuing sizable Treasury/MBS purchases is dovish forward guidance. Theory and evidence (Svensson and Woodford, 2003–2004) highlight that such guidance helps anchor expectations, while QE and liquidity facilities (Bernanke and coauthors; Federal Reserve on QE/forward guidance) ease financial conditions via term-structure channels consistent with Cochrane–Piazzesi. However, the signal that “a moderation in the pace of asset purchases may soon be warranted” is a mild hawkish tilt, and references to elevated (albeit considered transitory) inflation and virus risks temper optimism. On net, literature-consistent read is mildly positive but less upbeat than a purely dovish statement.
